note: Programme for the Japanese Day of Tea and Culture 2026. Programme subject to change.

items.title: Welcome
items.description: Welcome remarks from a representative of the Embassy of Japan in the Czech Republic, the City of Chýně and the event organiser.

items.title: Aikido Chýně
items.description: A demonstration of the traditional Japanese martial art of aikido.

items.title: Marek Hora
items.description: An ambassador of Japanese cuisine in the Czech Republic and an acclaimed chef in Europe and Japan. On stage, he will break down a fresh Hamachi and demonstrate expert sushi preparation.

items.title: Noriko Komiyama
items.description: A certified Sogetsu ikebana instructor. She will demonstrate the differences between two renowned schools — Ikenobo (池坊流) and Sogetsu (草月流) — and show how ordinary flowers can be turned into an impressive arrangement that visitors can also try at home.

items.title: Nihon Bunka Plzeň
items.description: A traditional kimono dressing demonstration. On stage, a representative of the City of Chýně will be dressed in kimono while the symbolism and purpose of each part of the outfit are explained.

items.title: Gorin
items.description: A samurai show featuring combat scenes inspired by the battlefields of the Sengoku period.

items.title: Aska Pluskal
items.description: A singer from Okinawa performs traditional and modern songs in Japanese.

items.title: Aikido Chýně
items.description: A second demonstration of the traditional Japanese martial art of aikido.

items.title: Iaido Plzeň
items.description: Demonstrations of the traditional Japanese martial art of iaido.

items.title: Kamigatamai – Markéta Franová
items.description: A traditional solo dance style from the Osaka and Kyoto region, characterised by elegance, restrained movement and subtle use of the fan.

items.title: Gorin – Samurai Archery
items.description: A samurai archery demonstration — a traditional Japanese discipline presented with live commentary.

items.title: Gorin – Tameshigiri
items.description: A tameshigiri demonstration — cutting rolled mats with a Japanese katana.
